title: Read this first
blocks: Shuttle Camera 0.1.39 - Installation and user guide - 18 October 2026
Capture PAL/NTSC VHS, play movie files, monitor Final Cut Pro or Premiere Pro, and send a Mac desktop through the Intensity Shuttle USB 3.0.

Experimental development build. The installer is unsigned; its components are ad-hoc signed and not notarized. The current installer requires SIP disabled. Read Security preparation before deciding to install. This is an independent project, not an official Blackmagic Design driver.
Apple-silicon Mac and macOS 27 or later. Testing was on one Mac Studio with macOS 27.0.1; other machines/releases are not comprehensively qualified.
Intensity Shuttle USB 3.0, working USB 3 cable/adapter, and administrator access. Intel Macs and the Thunderbolt Shuttle are not included.
VCR with S-Video or composite and RCA stereo for tape capture. A compatible TV/monitor or recorder for playback.

The Capture tab configures the camera feed; record with a separate camera app such as QuickTime Player. Video Output sends movies, editor frames or a desktop to the device. Capture and playback share the USB interface: use one at a time.

Live input picture adjustments, capture-resolution retention, idle pictures/movies with a delay, connector-format choices, desktop mirroring, experimental extended display, and Stretch that follows live desktop resolution changes.

The following pages cover security, installation, capture, Picture, movie output, Final Cut, Premiere, desktops, scaling, idle screens, audio/overlays, troubleshooting and removal. Screenshots are current native app views rendered with demonstration settings. They contain no personal footage; selected values are examples.

title: Security preparation
blocks: SIP protects macOS. Disabling it weakens protection across the Mac. Apple describes this as temporary development use; restore it after testing. Apple: disabling and enabling SIP.

Save work, back up important files and shut down. On Apple silicon, hold the power button until startup options appear. Choose Options > Continue and authenticate when requested. Apple: Recovery on Apple silicon.
In Recovery choose Utilities > Terminal. Run the following, then restart into normal macOS.
Check the status in normal Terminal:
The installer requires the fully disabled status; partial-disable combinations are not qualified. No supplied build script changes SIP. Building source alone does not require changing security.

Apple describes developer mode as relaxing the location check for extensions loaded outside normal application directories. The supplied installer puts the host in Applications. For developers reproducing the outside-Applications build setup, the command is: Apple: testing system extensions.
This is separate from screen-recording permission. Do not use it as a generic fix for camera or microphone access.

Use the removal/restoration steps at the end when finished. Continued operation after reenabling SIP has not been qualified for this ad-hoc build. This guide does not require disabling FileVault, authenticated-root protection or Gatekeeper globally, or enabling kernel extensions.

title: Install and enable
blocks: Obtain Shuttle-Capture-0.1.39.pkg from a trusted project release. The GitHub source-code ZIP is not the installer. Compare its SHA-256 with the release checksums.
Disable editor external output. Stop capture/playback and quit Shuttle Camera, the editors and camera apps.
Open the package, check that its heading says 0.1.39, and install on the current startup volume. Enter your administrator password in macOS when requested.

If macOS blocks an unsigned package, verify its source first. If you choose to proceed, use the specific package exception under Privacy & Security where offered; do not globally disable Gatekeeper. Apple: opening apps safely.
Open Shuttle Camera from Applications. Choose Help > Driver Setup > Enable Camera. For editor output, choose Enable HDMI Output.
Approve Shuttle Camera Extension and Shuttle HDMI Output Extension under System Settings > General > Login Items & Extensions > Camera Extensions.
Reopen Shuttle Camera and camera/editor clients after activation. Restart only if macOS requests it or the installed audio driver has not loaded.

An existing camera 17/output 12 installation does not need reactivation for this update. The installer backs up replaced bundles. An unchanged audio driver avoids a Core Audio restart; a first-time audio installation may briefly interrupt sound.
Compare the whole result with the matching release SHA256SUMS.txt. A checksum verifies file identity, not publisher trust or notarization.

title: Capture VHS
blocks: Capture controls with example PAL/S-Video settings. Match the cable and tape standard.
Connect VCR video OUT to the matching Shuttle input and red/white audio OUT to its RCA inputs. Connect USB 3 and play the tape.
Choose PAL or NTSC, the video input, Analog RCA, resolution and signal-loss behaviour. Close previews and click Apply.
In QuickTime choose File > New Movie Recording. Select the Shuttle camera and Intensity Shuttle - Stereo Audio microphone. Check picture, levels and a short recording before a long transfer.

PAL sizes: native 720x576, square 768x576, 1280x960 or 1440x1080. NTSC: native 720x480, square 640x480, 1280x960 or 1440x1080. Larger 4:3 sizes are scaled and add no tape detail. Bob deinterlacing gives 50 fps PAL / approximately 59.94 fps NTSC.
Hold last frame or Black preserves capture timing during signal loss; it cannot repair an unstable tape signal. Apply commits format changes. Refresh reloads the active camera settings.

title: Live picture controls
blocks: Picture controls update the camera feed while a preview is open.
Start the VCR and open the capture preview. In Picture, leave Live adjustments enabled.
Adjust Brightness, Contrast, Colour (saturation) and Sharpness. Watch the preview while moving a slider.
Use Reset picture for neutral processing. Check your recording before committing a long transfer.

These are software input-picture adjustments, applied to the camera feed rather than the tape. They do not control HDMI playback colour format. Changing video standard/input/resolution still needs Apply with previews closed.
If controls are unavailable, use Capture > Refresh. An older active camera extension may require activation with previews closed. Do not keep clicking Enable when the current driver is already ready.

title: Movie playback and formats
blocks: Choose a movie, select Fit/Fill/Stretch and optionally loop it. The filename is illustrative.
Close camera previews. Select Movie file, click Choose movie and select an output connector and format.
Select sizing, enable Loop if desired and click Start output. Use Stop when finished. The movie supplies its own sound; Use Shuttle Audio is not required for it.

S-Video and composite use PAL/NTSC. HDMI/component keep supported SD/HD formats. Compatible connectors may remain active together; the selection constrains formats, not an exclusive switch. Separate HD-plus-downconverted-SD output is not implemented.

title: Final Cut Pro output
blocks: Final Cut output settings and monitoring controls; example values are shown.
Choose Final Cut Pro and a format appropriate to the timeline. Click Use Shuttle Audio if sound should follow the device.
Click Start Final Cut and wait for Ready for Final Cut. Keep Shuttle Camera open.
In Final Cut Pro 11, choose Settings > Playback > A/V Output > Intensity Shuttle - HDMI Output. Enable Window > A/V Output and play or scrub.
When finished, disable Final Cut A/V Output first, then Stop in Shuttle Camera. Turning A/V Output off alone does not restore the Mac sound route.

The Shuttle output is SD/HD, not 4K. Rendering/downscaling of a 4K timeline takes place in the editor. Compare the same section with A/V Output off if playback becomes choppy, and check timeline/output cadence before changing driver settings.

title: Premiere Pro output
blocks: Premiere source selection. Video and audio are selected separately in Premiere.
Choose Premiere Pro and the matching format. Click Start Premiere and wait for Ready for Premiere.
In Premiere Pro 2025 Playback settings enable Mercury Transmit and the video stream for Intensity Shuttle - HDMI Output.
In Audio Hardware > Default Output select Intensity Shuttle - HDMI Audio. The Transmit plug-in is video-only; an empty audio-stream column is expected.
Disable Mercury Transmit before stopping output. Restore any explicit Premiere audio-device selection inside Premiere itself.

Restart Premiere after plug-in installation. Its original Blackmagic Playback entry is separate from this project. If output disappears in the background, check Premiere's Disable video output when in the background option. Close one editor's external output before using another.

title: Mirror or extend the desktop
blocks: Extended display with Stretch selected. Start creates a separate Mac desktop.
Choose Mac desktop to mirror an existing screen, or Extended display for a separate desktop. Select connector, video format and sizing.
Grant Screen & System Audio Recording permission to Shuttle Camera in Privacy & Security when requested; reopen the app afterwards.
Start output. For Extended display, arrange Shuttle Extended Display in macOS Displays, then drag windows onto it. Use Shuttle Audio if Mac media sound should follow it.
Stop removes the virtual display and restores the saved audio route.

PAL/NTSC start with a 1024x768 desktop scaled to SD; HD starts with 1920x1080. macOS may offer other desktop sizes. The virtual desktop uses 60 Hz and is sampled into the selected video cadence. It is not a direct GPU monitor connection.

Extended display uses an undocumented macOS interface and may change after an OS update. Protected media may not be capturable. ScreenCaptureKit captures video here; audio uses the separate Core Audio route.

title: Fit, Fill and Stretch
blocks: Keeps the whole image and its proportions; adds borders when needed.
Fills without distortion by cropping the edges.
Maps the whole image into the whole output frame; proportions can change.
Change desktop resolutions while output runs
Stop output and choose Stretch in Video Output, then start it.
Select the virtual/mirrored screen in macOS Displays and choose a desktop resolution. The whole current screen now fills the fixed video frame without restarting the sender.
For Fit/Fill, restart output after changing desktop resolution so their preserved-aspect geometry is recalculated.

Live software tests covered all eleven requested desktop sizes into HD, PAL and NTSC output surfaces: 1920x1080, 1600x1200, 1600x900, 1344x1008, 1344x756, 1280x960, 1280x720, 1024x768, 1024x576, 960x540 and 800x600. Available choices depend on the screen.

A 4:3 desktop stretched to 16:9 becomes wider. This is intentional Stretch behaviour. Desktop resolution, capture resolution and physical video timing are three different settings. Choosing a larger desktop does not add 4K or 1080p50/60 Shuttle wire output.

The same sizing choices are available for movie playback and idle pictures/movies. Restart output after changing idle sizing or media. The software accounts for PAL/NTSC pixel proportions when calculating Fit/Fill.

title: Choose an idle screen
blocks: Example idle picture using the original project icon, with a two-minute delay.
In Idle Screen, choose Hold last frame, Black, Colour bars, Picture or Movie loop (silent).
Use Choose media for a picture/movie. Choose Fit/Fill/Stretch and a Show after delay.
Restart output to apply the saved choice. Keep output running; playback or scrubbing restores new editor video immediately.

The default is two minutes without newly received editor frames. Delay choices are Immediately, 30 seconds, 1/2/5/10 minutes or Never. This replaces idle editor output, not a camera input-loss picture.

An idle movie loops silently. Keep the original movie file available at its saved location; an imported still is copied to Application Support. Missing/unreadable media falls back to black with a diagnostic.

title: Sound, sync and overlays
blocks: Use Shuttle Audio in Shuttle Camera
Intensity Shuttle - HDMI Audio in Audio Hardware
Sound from the selected movie file

Use Shuttle Audio changes the Mac media output and saves its previous selection. Stop, helper exit or app quit restores it while the route is still the Shuttle; a later manual change is respected. Compatible device outputs can carry sound, though the Core Audio device keeps its existing HDMI Audio name. An explicit Premiere selection must be restored in Premiere.

Negative values move sound earlier; positive values delay it. Range: -100 to +500 ms, with 10 ms stepper increments. Press Return after typing a value and compare after about a second. Reset returns to zero. This is for timeline output, not capture recording; adjustments can briefly click or skip.
Timecode: TC HH:MM:SS:FF, or a semicolon for drop-frame. Dashes mean the editor supplied no valid timecode.
L/R meters: outgoing stereo levels, peak hold and clip indication.
Positions: six choices each for timecode and meters, with independent placement. The timecode background is translucent.
Title safe 80% / Action safe 90%: optional white/yellow guides. These are app guide percentages, not a broadcaster-compliance guarantee.

Overlays affect the outgoing picture on compatible outputs, not the editor project/source file. Output timecode is for editors; meters/guides also work with movie playback. About and Quit are in the app menu; Help contains setup, diagnostics and driver actions.

title: Troubleshooting
blocks: Quit editors/camera apps and stop output. Confirm the installer heading/version; use the startup volume. Installer Log gives the actual failure.
Enable Camera in Help > Driver Setup and approve Camera Extensions; reopen the recording app.
Choose the separate Stereo Audio microphone, Analog RCA input and microphone permission.
Quit Shuttle Camera. Remove its old Screen & System Audio Recording entry, add /Applications/Shuttle Camera.app again, enable and reopen. Ad-hoc updates can leave an old permission signature.
Select Extended display and Start. Use current software; PAL/NTSC now start at 1024x768. Test pattern does not create a desktop.
Only part of a desktop shows
Stop, select Stretch, start again. Stretch follows live desktop size changes; restart Fit/Fill after a mode change.
Match timeline/output cadence; compare A/V Output off/on. Check rendering/media load and collect diagnostics during the affected session.
The tested Dell P2213t needs YPbPr for HDMI-to-DVI. Selectable RGB output is not implemented.
Restore audio in Shuttle Camera or Sound settings; restore explicit Premiere output inside Premiere.
Restart Premiere and confirm the Transmit bundle is in the legacy Plug-ins path listed on the next page.

For a report, include app/macOS/editor versions, project/source frame rate, output format, connection and relevant diagnostics. Review logs for personal filenames. Every codec, 4K timeline, analogue combination and long-session latency has not been comprehensively qualified. There is no Resolve output integration or simultaneous capture/playback.

title: Remove it and restore security
blocks: Save work. Disable editor external output, stop playback/capture, restore sound and quit clients.
Use Help > Driver Setup > Disable Camera. Turn off both Shuttle Camera Extensions in System Settings.
Move Shuttle Camera.app from Applications to the Bin. Allow macOS to remove bundled extensions if prompted. Do not manually delete /Library/SystemExtensions.
In Finder, move only this project's audio driver and Premiere bundle at the paths below to the Bin. Administrator approval may be required. Restart to unload audio and finish pending removal.
Source, status and backups: <font name="Courier">/Library/Application Support/Shuttle Camera</font>. User settings/media are under the user's Library/Application Support/Shuttle Camera.
If developer mode was enabled, turn it off in normal Terminal:
In Recovery Terminal, reenable SIP and restart. Verify with csrutil status in normal macOS. Apple: disabling and enabling SIP.

The ad-hoc extensions may stop working with SIP restored; this runtime configuration is not qualified. Do not reset all system extensions, because that affects unrelated software. Keep backups until normal audio and files are checked.
